items.prescription: The two levers this loop has already named are still the right ones, and neither is a loosened floor. Preferred: build the content-ratio fallback the iter-09 addendum declined for want of a validated threshold - but validate it by MEASUREMENT rather than by heuristic, which is what made it undeliverable last round. Render all 495 entries once in a headless pass, record .prose and .entry-side heights for each, and pick the threshold from the resulting distribution; that is a single batch measurement, not a per-entry judgement, and it yields a threshold falsifiable in both directions the way the registry requires. Entries below it fall back to the single-column order S14 already validates. Alternative, if the distribution has no clean split: give this template a different mechanism than .home-grid's - the freed track holds narrow, tall content beside a long text body, which is a sidenote or margin-note shape rather than a two-column shape, and a template whose content does not fit the mechanism should change mechanism rather than have its floor lowered.

items.target: evidence rig (tools/ui-evidence.mjs freshness check) and JUDGE.md L6
items.problem: NEW, and I triggered it myself by following this loop's own instructions. L6 requires a judge to compare each capture's buildStamp against the tree before scoring and to treat a mismatch as FATAL. The stamp is a wall-clock timestamp emitted at build time, so it changes on every build whether or not any source changed. The judge is separately instructed to run npm run build as a gate. Doing both, in either order, guarantees a mismatch: the evidence set here records 2026-09-01T07:52:30Z and the tree now reads 2026-09-01T08:01:28Z, differing only because I ran the mandated build over an unmodified tree. A freshness oracle that cannot distinguish 'rebuilt with changes' from 'rebuilt with none' either forces a judge to recapture 40 images for nothing, or - far worse, and this is the real risk - teaches judges that L6 mismatches are routine and can be waved through, which is exactly how L1 became a blindfold before it was narrowed.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json buildStamp 2026-09-01T07:52:30Z against out/index.html data-build-stamp 2026-09-01T08:01:28Z after my gate run, with no source file edited by me at any point this session; tools/ui-evidence.mjs freshness assertion
items.invariant: The stamp compared for evidence freshness changes when and only when something that could alter the rendered artifact changes, so a rebuild over an unmodified tree leaves the evidence set valid.
items.governing_rule: JUDGE.md L6 - this is a defect in the known-lie's own remedy, not in the artifact
items.prescription: Emit a content hash beside the timestamp - a digest over the source inputs that determine the render (app/, lib/render/, content/, data/, globals.css) - and have the freshness check compare THAT, keeping the timestamp as human-readable metadata only. A no-op rebuild is then provably a no-op, and L6's fatal rule can stay fatal without producing false positives on any judge who follows the gate instructions. Amend L6's text at the same time to say which of the two fields it compares, since there would then be two.

items.prescription: Replace signature-matching with a direct comparison: after a fullPage capture, measure a handful of landmark elements' live bounding boxes and check that the captured image's dimensions are consistent with them. That detects the failure rather than predicting its cause - the same move R11's own post-mortem recommends for premises generally: verify the property, not the shape you expect it to take.

items.target: app/catalog page template (the ::before content attr(data-label) field labels at 390px) - keeper measurement
items.problem: Keeper-gate, carried, unchanged as a question and increasingly load-bearing as a blocker. Whether the generated-content field labels in the 390px stacked record form are announced by assistive technology is not answerable from axe-core, which is why it was correctly refused entry to the hard-measured accessibility category. It now blocks the only remaining CSS-safe route to reducing the 215.9px record height (I45), which is itself the mechanism behind the 102-screen scroll (I14). Three carried items now converge on one unperformed measurement.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/table-catalog--light--390.png (unreadable at 86,379px - see I44b); my own live measurement of the 215.9px record height; scripts/verify-design.mjs, which reports zero axe violations and cannot speak to this
items.prescription: Keeper measurement with a real screen reader on the 390px stacked form: are the ::before field labels announced, and in what relation to their values. The answer unblocks I45 and materially affects I14. It is the highest-leverage single measurement left in this loop's backlog, and it has been carried unperformed since iteration 2.

items.target: keeper - content gate (specs/directory's per-row provenance requirement vs /catalog's Read column)
items.problem: Keeper-gate, carried, unchanged. /catalog's Read column renders one identical date on 396 of 396 rows. I36 closed the weight half correctly and I re-verified it: the column renders at --muted in table-catalog--light--1440.png, visibly quieter than the model and numeric columns. The remaining half - that the column exists at all, repeating a constant 396 times - is blocked by specs/directory's per-row provenance requirement, which is a content decision. Noted here because I49 is the same defect on /tools where the content gate does NOT apply, and the pair makes the boundary of this loop's charter unusually legible.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/table-catalog--light--1440.png (READ column muted on every visible row); specs/directory's per-row provenance requirement; lib/catalog.mjs catalogRow doc comment
